title: Release: the canary gate reads a p99 that is not a p99, and promotion is at 14:00

objective: Histograms: _bucket, _sum and _count series, histogram_quantile over rate of buckets, and what a quantile estimate can and cannot tell you
secondaryObjectives: Writing readable queries: subqueries, recording-rule naming (level:metric:operations), and avoiding common PromQL mistakes

sources.cite: CNCF Prometheus Certified Associate (PCA) curriculum: PromQL 28%, Prometheus Fundamentals 20%, Observability Concepts 18%, Alerting & Dashboarding 18%, Instrumentation and Exporters 16%
sources.note: On 2026-11-17 the weights were confirmed through a third-party study page (kube-dojo.github.io/k8s/pca, summarizing fetch), which cites no curriculum version; the official curriculum (cncf/curriculum, read by the course builder for backend/supabase/seed/tracks/cncf-ecosystem.ts) was not re-read. The objective wording is the course seed's.

Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: the example 'histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) // GOOD.'; the _sum and _count series give the average of the observed values, not a quantile; with histograms 'the aggregation is perfectly possible', while aggregating summary quantiles 'rarely makes sense'. That a rate window needs at least two samples is general PromQL behavior not quoted from this page (to verify against the rate() function reference).

brief.situation: You are the on-call SRE for Larkspur Tickets, a fictional ticketing site. Checkout v2 is in a canary at 20% of traffic. At 13:30 support says some buyers wait seconds to pay, but the canary gate, a PromQL query in the rollout's analysis, reports p99 at 0.25 s against its 0.3 s limit. The rollout promotes v2 to 100% automatically at 14:00 if the gate passes.
handover: Prometheus scrapes checkout every 30 s; the latency metric is the histogram http_request_duration_seconds with a version label.
The gate query was written last week by copying a dashboard panel.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the canary, the gate and the traffic split.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The rollout's next step promotes at 14:00, 30 minutes after the report.

effects.finding: The gate runs histogram_quantile on raw cumulative bucket counters: no rate over a window and no sum by le. It reads counts since each pod started, not recent latency.

effects.finding: A 30 s scrape gives one sample per 30 s: a rate window must hold at least two samples, so [30s] is often empty and [5m] holds about ten.

then.output:

{{version="v1"}} => 0.21
{{version="v2"}} => 1.84

then.log: Summing the per-second rate of buckets by le, per version, gives v2's p99 over the last 5 minutes: 1.84 s.

then.output:
sre@obs:~$ promtool query instant http://prometheus:9090 'histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[30s]))'
Empty query result (most series) / NaN

then.log: A 30 s window over a 30 s scrape rarely holds two samples, and without sum by le each pod's buckets stand alone.
That is the mean. The slow 1-2% of requests hardly move it.

writeup.question: For the record: why the gate passed, what v2's p99 really was, and what you did about the release.

parts.label: Why it passed
parts.criteria: Names what is wrong with the gate's query.
parts.modelAnswer: histogram_quantile needs the per-second rate of each bucket over a window, summed by le: the gate fed it raw cumulative counters per series, so it read history since the pods started, not current latency.

parts.label: Real p99
parts.criteria: Writes the correct query with a window that fits the 30 s scrape, and does not settle for a mean.
parts.modelAnswer: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, version)(rate(..._bucket[5m]))) gave v1 0.21 s and v2 1.84 s; the mean was 0.19 s and hides the tail; a [30s] window is too short for a 30 s scrape.

parts.label: Release
parts.criteria: Stops the promotion before 14:00 and fixes the gate for next time.
parts.modelAnswer: Aborted the rollout so v1 took all traffic, fixed the gate's query and added a recording rule the dashboard and gate share.

promotedSlow.headline: Promoted on a number that was not a p99
promotedSlow.body: histogram_quantile over raw cumulative buckets reads history, not recent latency, and without sum by le each series stands alone. The correct query showed v2 at 1.84 s.

scoring.modelReasoning: The gate runs histogram_quantile on the raw bucket counters: they are cumulative since each pod started, there is no rate over a window, and without sum by le each series is estimated alone, so it reports an old, flattering number. The right p99 is histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, version)(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))): v2 is at 1.84 s. A [30s] window over a 30 s scrape rarely holds the two samples rate needs, and _sum over _count is the mean, which hides the tail. Abort the canary so v1 serves everyone, fix the gate's query, and add a recording rule named level:metric:operations that the dashboard and the gate share. Silencing the alert only hides the one true signal.
